subject: Deployment segregation blueprint for Private/Dedicated - Bluewave Security Request
messages:
From: Asha Varma <asha.varma@bluewavehealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Bluewave Security Team <security@bluewavehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: deployment segregation blueprint + assurance artifacts

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the conversation earlier this week. As part of our internal vendor risk evaluation we're asking for a concise "deployment segregation blueprint" that covers how Redwood isolates customer workloads across Dedicated and Private modes. Specifically we're interested in:

- Control plane / data plane separation: logical and network boundaries, where control traffic terminates, and how we ensure control plane metadata doesn't cross customer VPCs.
- Network paths for tenant ingress/egress (including default-deny posture, egress proxies, and approved outbound endpoints).
- Layering for host/VM/container isolation (e.g., microVMs, sidecar proxies, hypervisor attestation).
- Key management boundaries and KMS transit assumptions for Private deployments.
- Evidence we can validate: high-level diagrams, an isolation matrix mapping, and sample flow logs or retention windows.

Can you provide a single-slide diagram plus a short spreadsheet/matrix and any sample logs you can share (redacted)? We're on a tight review cadence and would appreciate anything by EOD Monday (2027-04-05). If there are items that must remain under NDA, call them out and we can route accordingly.

Best,
Asha Varma
Senior InfoSec Manager
Bluewave Health

Attachments: vendor-questionnaire-bluewave.pdf (referenced)

- Kim: please produce the isolation matrix (sheet showing: component, tenancy model (shared/dedicated/customer-VPC), network controls, attestation/PKI, audit evidence available). Include a column listing what we can share without an NDA and what requires an LOE/NDA.
- Priya: if you can collect a redacted example of flow logs and proof of retention policy we can attach.

I'll consolidate into a single bundle and reply to Asha. Deadline: EOD Mon (2027-04-05).

Thanks — Vivek

Vivek / Kim — quick clarifications as I build the diagram and matrix:

1) Control plane variants: we should show three patterns — Hosted-Shared (Redwood-managed control plane for Hosted API), Hosted-Dedicated (control plane in Redwood but reserved networking), and Private (customer-managed control plane in their VPC or on-prem). For Private we will annotate the optional bridge appliance (thin VM that provides NAT and reverse-tunnel).
2) Tenant isolation primitives: include per-tenant workload groups (cgroups/containers), optional microVMs (firecracker), and per-tenant sidecar proxies for egress filtering.
3) Egress posture: default-deny with enforced egress proxy in both Dedicated and Private unless the customer requests route-based peering. Document the approved outbound endpoints (e.g., KMS endpoints, metrics sink, telemetry collector) and how we IP allow-list.
4) Attestation and keys: note HSM-backed KMS for Redwood-managed KMS, and customer-managed KMS for Private. Include statement re: hardware attestation for appliances if deployed on-customer-prem.
5) Audit artifacts: we can provide flow logs (VPC flow logs format), connection-level proxy logs (redacted), and configuration snapshots; retention standard 90 days by default, extendable to 365 under contract.

I'll attach: redwood-deployment-segregation-v1.svg and isolation-matrix-bluewave.xlsx in the next message. Anything else to call out to Bluewave?

- Karthik
Senior Cloud Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Asha / team — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching the bundle requested:

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood-deployment-segregation-v1.svg (single-slide diagram; shows control/data plane separation, private bridge placement, and egress proxies)
- isolation-matrix-bluewave.xlsx (component-by-component tenancy and evidence mapping; column for shareable vs NDA)
- control-plane-flow.txt (sample, redacted connection flow log; timestamps and IPs redacted)

High level summary we included in the slide and matrix:
- Control plane: For Hosted and Dedicated the control plane is Redwood-managed. For Private we support a customer-controlled control plane (deployed in customer VPC) with an optional thin bridge appliance for environments that cannot accept inbound connections. Cryptographic keys for Redwood-managed control plane are HSM-backed; customers can bring own KMS for Private installations.
- Network segregation: Default-deny egress enforced via sidecar proxies. For Dedicated we use reserved subnets plus routing policies to ensure tenant blast radius is minimized. For Private we call out the boundary where traffic transitions to customer routing.
- Evidence: flow logs (VPC flow logs / NAT gateway logs), proxy connection logs, and infrastructure configuration snapshots. Standard retention 90 days; contractual extension available.
- Items that require NDA: detailed hypervisor attestation artifacts, full unredacted logs, and customer-specific appliance images.

Next steps: Vivek/Karthik/Priya will provide a short cover note (one page) that contextualizes the artifacts for Bluewave's vendor review; we can escalate anything that Bluewave marks as high-risk.

Kimberly Park
Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
